clinician.final_diagnosis: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML), chronic phase, BCR/ABL positive
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 53-year-old incarcerated male presented 4 days after abdominal trauma with focal peritonitis, marked leukocytosis (WBC 38.4 × 10^9/L), and thrombocytosis (platelets 691 × 10^9/L). CT imaging revealed a pancreatic hematoma with hemoperitoneum requiring acute surgical management. However, the degree of leukocytosis and thrombocytosis, combined with constitutional symptoms (fatigue, easy bruising, spontaneous epistaxis) and a 2-month history of vague abdominal pain predating the trauma, prompted hematologic evaluation. Peripheral blood smear confirmed severe leukocytosis and thrombocytosis without circulating blasts, effectively ruling out acute leukemia. Bone marrow biopsy performed after positive PCR testing demonstrated slightly hypercellular marrow (70%) with trilineage hematopoiesis, mild myeloid hyperplasia, and mild megakaryocytic hyperplasia—morphology consistent with a myeloproliferative neoplasm. The temporal sequence (bone marrow biopsy performed 'after PCR positive') combined with initiation of imatinib 400mg daily (a BCR/ABL-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor) confirms molecular evidence of BCR/ABL fusion. The patient showed hematologic response to therapy with WBC normalizing from 38.4 to 11.6 × 10^9/L at discharge.
